messages:
emma: Heads up — we're getting a sharp spike of 502/504s for hosted inference from customers in eu-west1 (primarily az-b). Started ~08:23 UTC, error rate ~18% on gateway. Customers reporting timeouts and partial responses.

javier: looking at edge metrics now. I see increased packet loss on the az-b interconnect (egress) and a bunch of retransmits. BGP updates around 08:22:12 from provider 20345.

kai: can you paste the mtr/traceroute? also any correlation with deploys?

emma: no deploys around that time, deploy-bot shows last deploy 06:10. here's a quick mtr from an affected edge host -> customer pop: ```
Start: 08:25:03
1. 10.10.0.1 0.4% 1ms
2. transit-asm-1 7.8% 12ms
3. provider-20345 16.7% 38ms
4. eu-west1-edge 18.3% 45ms
```

javier: yep provider hop is showing microbursts and packet loss. interface counters show FEC/CRC errors on transit port, provider confirms they were seeing a brief flapping link and BGP AS path changes (withdraws then re-advertise).

sara-cs: multiple customers opened tickets, three flagged as P1 (latency + runtime crashes). CS wants ETA and mitigation notes to send to customers.

linda-cs: I'm on the calls. Customers want repro steps we can give them and any mitigation (eg. failover region) we recommend.

emma: quick mitigation plan: 1) shift routed traffic for hosted inference to backup transit in eu-west1 (policy fallback) 2) for customers with cross-region tolerance, recommend switching to eu-west2 copy (we can update routing policy per-tenant) 3) open provider ticket and request expedited HW swap.

kai: I pushed a temporary routing policy to send new sessions to backup transit (policy id: rbk-98). Applying canary for 10% now then 50%.

incident-bot: action_log: routing_policy_apply rbk-98 by kai at 08:29:40 UTC -> canary 10%

javier: provider just confirmed a partial fiber cut at their POP, they're provisioning an alternate path. BGP instability until new path is in place. Expect flaps for ~30-45m.

emma: monitoring note: token-level errors decreased from 18% -> 6% after canary. still seeing tail latency spikes for some long-running inference calls (kv-cache warmups).

sara-cs: relayed mitigation to customers: use eu-west2 or wait 45m while we failover. Some customers asked for manual re-routing of their tenant to eu-west2 — can we do that?

kai: we can update tenant routing for Hosted API; I'll run a mapping job. ETA ~12m for bulk re-route and validation.

javier: creating provider ticket: TT-20345-8471 (shared with ops). Also filing internal incident with network team.

emma: repro steps for support docs: 1) trigger large batched request to hosted inference in eu-west1 2) observe repeated 502s and `gateway: upstream read timeout` logs 3) run `mtr -r -c 50 <edge-ip>` and look for >5% loss at provider hop 4) collect pod-level logs: `kubectl logs -l app=hosted-inference -n prod --since=10m` and attach.

linda-cs: copying that into customer-facing note. adding suggested temporary workaround: reduce max parallel requests to 2 and enable client retries with exponential backoff.

emma: added runbook step: if provider loss persists >15m escalate to on-call network lead and request BGP prepull/ARP flush on edge.

kai: re-route job finished for three tenants (ids t-412, t-893, t-1102). verified successful calls against eu-west2 after reroute.

incident-bot: metric_alert: gateway_5xx_rate dropped below threshold at 08:41:02 UTC -> resolved (partial).

javier: provider reports alternate path up, CRC counters stable. I'll keep monitoring for 2h.

emma: next steps: - CS to notify customers with timeline + mitigation steps (linda/sara) - network to confirm full restore (javier) - infra to keep canary routing for 30m then revert (kai).

sara-cs: sending update now. thanks all. :thumbsup:

linda-cs: note for postmortem: include time series of gateway latencies, packet loss at provider hop, customer tickets opened, and exact tenant reroute timestamps.

javier: logging raw pcap for 15m window starting 08:20 -> saved to /var/tmp/pcap-eu-west1-0819.pcap for SRE analysis.

emma: closing loop in thread — feel free to ping if it flares back up.
